title: mass effect
text: An amazing space opera packed with action. True, the side quests can become a bit annoying and repetitive but some of them (if finished) will reward you in Mass Effect 2 or 3. Not reward in a full sence of words but you'll get kind of easter eggs and meet those characters in other games. The graphics are a bit outdated but that should not stop you to enjoy this epic chase around the galaxy for a rogue spectre. There are certain mods to enhance your experience of course. The gameplay in ME1 is more of an RPG style than in ME2 and 3 and you need to think more strategicaly and tacticaly. The biggest thing that bothers me in this game is how the Mako (vehicle) is so hard to control and the controls are just sloppy (but fear not there is also a mod for that). Of course there is not only action but romance in this game (if you wish to have a romance, you're not obligated). Anyway, I finished this game probably more than 5 times already and it never stops to amaze me. P.S. Don't choose the engineer as your class.

title: mass effect
text: A captivating RPG which really lets you make your own choices that carry through the whole story. In Mass Effect, you don't play as Commander Shepard; you are Commander Shepard. The first installment of the series boasts an immersive plot that makes you want to learn the rest of the story right away. Mass Effect world is based on amazing amount of lore, available in game in form of 'codex entries', creating a complex and self-consistent universe almost comparable to that of the Star Wars saga. Add to that extensive dialogues, literally dozens of explorable planets and exciting combat, and you get the glimpse of why ME is so compelling. It's a game enjoyable for both die-hard RPG fans and newcomers. The equipment system with its stats and the sheer amount of items might be a bit overwhelming at the beginning, but it's easy to get used to; same goes for the leveling system. Fight itself is not very complicated, but those who seek a challenge will definitely find it on higher difficulty levels. Mass Effect power system makes enemy encounters more than just simple firefights, and you can choose from several squadmates with unique skills to tackle different kinds of enemies. Still, the power of Mass Effect lies mainly in dialogues and player decisions. This is why ME (and the trilogy as a whole) holds such a big replayable value - by making different choices, you can complete several playthroughs and still encounter new parts of the game. By completing side quests (or, in Mass Effect terminology, asssignments) you get some 40 to 50 hours of the game, even though the main storyline can be completed pretty quickly. But that's not the point, is it? Don't forget to download the free 'Bring Down the Sky' DLC and enjoy! This might well become your favourite franchise, as it is mine.

title: mass effect 2
text: Mass Effect 2 (ME2) is the sequel to the amazing Mass Effect (ME1). In Mass Effect 2, you play as Commander Shepard and recruit 12 powerful squad members (2 from DLCs) in your team to fight against the enemies. Compared to ME1, the features in ME2 have been tremendously improved and polished. Since I have played ME1, expect to find a few comparisons in this game review. - Breathtaking cinematic cutscenes (So many feelings and goosebumps) - Beautiful music (More goosebumps) - Skippable conversations - Character and armor customization - Great story, unforgettable ending - Additional squad members (badass, mysterious, crazy, and funny individuals) - Same ammo used for all weapons (except heavy weapons) - Improved HUD screen and power wheel - Squad movements associated with key bindings (no more via HUD) - Enemies protections are color coded (barrier - purple, shields - yellow, armor and health red) - Space/Galaxy exploration - Progress status on space exploration - Interesting dialogs (Some of them are funny) - Shorter loading time - Purchasable mementos and pets for your cabin - No more annoying elevators - Two mini-puzzle to unlock research and credits - Any classes can hack now (not only techies) - A few intense time limited missions - Missions can be continued after finishing the main plot - Pursue a romantic relationship - In-depth encyclopedia (Codex) - Arrow pointer in map - Tutorial at the start of the game - Introduction to newer species (Drell, Batarians, Vorcha) and creatures - Variety of alien species and enemies - Emphasize teamwork - Access to Cerberus Network (You'll get extra weapons, armor, missions and one more squad member) - Fewer skills/abilities (but it is fine since you have many squad members) - Weapons stats no longer exist (but weapons can be made stronger via research) - Specific weapons for specific classes (e.g. Infiltrator cannot use assault rifle) (but preferable than those in ME1 where weapon’s accuracy was affected) - Difficulty in reaching level 30 (possible if ME1 character is imported, completed all missions and DLCs, or continue a new game after first playthrough)  - Other expensive DLCs (you'll need Bioware points to purchase them) - DLCs not sold in Steam - Mako missions replaced with probes - Possible wastage on buying probes and fuel (I did) - Scanning planets could be dull and repetitive over time - No running, only sprinting - The "Press 'F' to Finish Mission" blocked the dialog wheel - Failure to connect to Mass Effect 2 server error (popped up every single time after starting the game) Overall, the good outweighs the bad in Mass Effect 2. If you are a fan of Mass Effect or if you love action role-playing, sci-fi adventure and exploration, then this game is for you. Mass Effect 2 will definitely be one of the games where you will cherish the feel good moment. You will wish to replay it in the future to experience those nostalgic moments again. Note: Be prepared to feel empty after you have finished playing this game because I do. A tip for those who are reading until this far, pay a visit to Uranus and launch a probe if you have not already.

If you are fortunate enough the play the first Mass Effect prior to this one, you can import your save and the choices from that game affect this one!  The controls are solid and the visuals are great.  I highly recommend this title.

text: I already didn't recommend Any other DooM release on Steam with the same review Copy-pasted because of the same problems. But this one deserves its own review. A little statement first. As already mentioned in my other DooM reviews the 0/10 rate is related to the Steam Release. Consider that I grew up with doom, I was 6 years old when the shareware was being widespread all over the world, and still nowadays I own The original DooM, DooM II and The Ultimate Collection DooM 95 (With Ultimate DooM, DooM II And Final DooM). All of this to state I know and Love the game I grew up with. Despite all this I regret to NOT Recommend this RELEASE (Not THE GAME, mind you). On a Side note: all the DooM chapters have been released on Steam like this, so I'm not recommending Any other chapter, specifically The Ultimate DooM, Final DooM And DooM II: Hell On Earth. My same Review will be posted in all those releases because of the same flaws. This Master Levels For DooM II release is supposed to have a total of 21 maps (including the "Teeth" Secret level) AND 1830 amateur custom levels. What does this release have? 21 Maps... Don't tell me the 1830 maps would weight too much, wad files have a ridiculous size. Anyways, to play the 21 maps you'll have to stick with an outdated and sometimes stuttering version of dosbox running the game with the already mentioned and useless "modern controls". Too bad that now you can't select a classic control system. Top of the Tops you still have to use that outdated, NON-user friendly ridiculous text-interface to select the map to play with. Meaning you don't get to play the 21 maps one after the other, but you have to select which map replace the original DooM II map. So this means you will get to play again some DooM II levels (21, replacing 32). And that's not the worst part. The maps have the "replacing slot locked" and most of them replace the same slot... BUT WHY?!?!? And if this wasn't enough You are FORCED to use the "Modern Interface" set as default in the other DooM Steam releases. But here you can't revert to the Classic interface. Definitley the worst release Ever. Fortunately this is a bonus pack for those brave or squanderer enough to buy these horrible releases. I'll just copy-paste the cons of the other releases, which still apply on this one. It's not worth a total rewrite...
